answer: A bridge bond is a strong defense: for market entry, an agent locks a stake in escrow, returned only after honest behavior is proven. The stake is priced so one agent can afford it but a thousand fake identities cannot, since each clone multiplies the cost. Reputation then grows like saffron, slowly: every verified job adds a small earned credential, so fresh identities start at zero trust. Honest agents form a verifying oasis, checking work history before paying. Flooding it means paying the bond per fake identity and waiting out the slow growth, so the attack costs more than it could steal.
